notes: 2026 bracket thresholds are from Oregon DOR's 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE rate charts and the 2026 withholding formulas (Charts S and J); heads of household use the joint chart. The 2026 Form OR-40 has not been published yet.

2026 standard deduction ($2,910 / $5,820 / $4,685) is from the DOR 2026 Combined Payroll Tax Report instructions and withholding formulas; the earlier OR-ESTIMATE publication listed estimates of $2,900 / $5,800 / $4,650. Confirm against the 2026 OR-40 instructions when released.
Personal exemption credit is $263 per exemption in the 2026 withholding formulas (OR-ESTIMATE estimated $260). Modeled as $0 when AGI exceeds $100,000 (single) or $200,000 (joint, head of household).

Oregon subtracts federal income tax liability (2026 limit $8,750, $4,375 MFS), phased out between $125,000 and $145,000 AGI (single) or $250,000 and $290,000 (joint/HoH). Modeled with a straight-line phase-out (Oregon uses steps).

Additional standard deduction for age 65+/blind, Oregon itemized deductions, the reduced pass-through rate for qualified business income (requires employees), kicker credit, Working Family Household and Dependent Care credit and other credits are not modeled.

Self-employed people working in the TriMet or Lane Transit districts owe a separate transit self-employment tax (TriMet 0.8237%, LTD 0.80% of net SE earnings over $400, Forms OR-TM / OR-LTD); not modeled.

seDeduction.note: Oregon starts from federal AGI; DOR says the half-SE-tax deduction flows through and needs no separate Oregon entry for full-year residents.

seHealthInsurance.note: DOR says the federal self-employed health insurance deduction flows through federal AGI for full-year residents.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) contributions deducted for federal AGI carry through to Oregon.

qbi.note: Oregon is disconnected from the IRC § 199A QBI deduction (ORS 316.859); it does not flow to the Oregon return.

localIncomeTax.note: Portland-area residents with high incomes owe Metro Supportive Housing Services tax (1% of taxable income over $128,000 single / $205,000 joint for 2026) and Multnomah County Preschool for All tax (1.5% over $125,000 single / $200,000 joint, plus another 1.5% over $250,000 / $400,000; PFA thresholds unchanged for 2026; Metro SHS thresholds indexed to $128,000 / $205,000). Quarterly estimates are required from 2026 when either tax exceeds $5,000. These apply to a minority of residents and are not modeled. TriMet/LTD transit self-employment taxes are noted under income tax notes.

localities.note: Metro SHS: 1% of Oregon taxable income over $128,000 (single) or $205,000 (joint and head of household) for 2026. Multnomah PFA: 1.5% over $125,000 single / $200,000 joint, plus 1.5% more over $250,000 / $400,000. Portland does not state the PFA threshold for head of household; the single threshold is used here. The $35 Portland Arts Tax is not included.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you expect to owe $1,000 or more of Oregon tax after credits and withholding.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Required annual payment is the lesser of 90% of 2026 tax after credits or 100% of 2025 tax after credits (2025 return must be filed and not a short year). Annualized installments allowed via Form OR-10.
estimatedTax.form: Form OR-40-V (estimated payment voucher) or Revenue Online; see Publication OR-ESTIMATE

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $100 Articles of Organization (Oregon Secretary of State Corporation Division).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $100 annual report/renewal for a domestic LLC, due every year on the anniversary of registration.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None for income tax purposes. Corporate Activity Tax (CAT) applies only above $1 million of Oregon commercial activity: $250 plus 0.57% of taxable commercial activity over $1 million (registration required at $750,000).
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: Oregon Corporate Activity Tax applies to sole proprietors and LLCs alike, but only when Oregon commercial activity exceeds $1 million (registration at $750,000). Most freelancers are below this.
